The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Karan Malhotra suffered grievous injury.
texts.facts: 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Karan Malhotra suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 06.08.2018 at about 9 am, Petitioner was riding a Motorcycle No. DL-13-SU-9653 with his friend(Dheeraj Joshi,since deceased in the accident) from NOIDA to Ghaziabad. When they reached opposite Maya Farm House, Vijay Nagar, Ghaziabad, their vehicle was hit from behind by one Dumper No.UP-16-ET-1197(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle). Due to the impact, pillion rider Dheeraj Joshi died while the petitioner received grievous injuries. Petitioner was removed to Flores hospital, Ghaizabad, thereafter to Fortis Hospital NOIDA and finally shifted to Kailash hospital, NOIDA for treatment. 3. An FIR bearing no.1194/2018 dated 06.08.2018 u/s 279,338,304A IPC PS Vijay Nagar, District-Ghaziabad, U.P. was registered against Respondent no.1. After investigation, chargesheet was filed in the court of concerned Ld. Magistrate and a claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 2 of 25 BK 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, Respondent no.2 is the owner and Respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the petition, Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply denying their liability to compensate the injured. It has been pleaded that the accident was not caused due to the negligence of Respondent no.1. It is further pleaded that Respondent no.1 was having valid driving licence and the vehicle was duly insured with Respondent no.3. On the other hand, Respondent no.3 has denied its liability in case of breach of any of the condition of the insurance police including lack of driving licence or a valid permit or fitness. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 04.06.2019. OPP. 3. Relief. Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 2 7. In order to prove its case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW- 1/A, reiterating the averments of his petition. He further stated that the injury sustained in the accident resulted in amputation of the right mid arm of PW-1 apart from other multiple injuries. He stated that the IPD expenses of Kailash Hospital, NOIDA were reimbursed by his mother through her ESI card. He relied upon MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 3 of 25 BK medical bills amounting to Rs.11,82,959/- as Ex.PW-1/1, discharge summary from Fortis hospital as Mark-1, MLC from Fortis hospital as Mark-2, discharge summary from Kailash hospital Ex.PW-1/2, disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/3, quotation of artificial limb as Ex.PW-1/4, 10th class marksheet as Ex.PW-1/5, 12th class marksheet as Ex.PW-1/6, marksheet of first semester of B.Tech as Ex.PW-1/7, driving licence of PW-1 as Ex.PW-1/8, his bank passbook as Ex.PW-1/9, his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/10, his PAN card Ex.PW-1/11, certificate regarding one year study loss as Ex.PW-1/12, placement summary as Ex.PW-1/13, prescription for physiotherapy as Ex.PW-1/14, medical bills of treatment amounting to Rs.6,651/- as Ex.PW- 1/15 and counselling summary for future expenses issued by BLK Memorial hospital as Ex.PW-1/16. He was duly cross- examined by learned counsel for R-3/insurance company. Sh. Manoj Kumar Sharma (Assistant Registrar, J.P. Institute of Information Technology) was examined as PW- 2(inadvertently noted as PW-3). He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.PW-3/1, admission and placement record of the injured as Ex.PW-3/2, His ID card as Ex.PW-3/4, copy of forwarded e-mail sent by Anita Marwah, Senior officer, Training and Placement Officer, JIIT as Ex.PW-3/5. He deposed that the injured had received job offer from three companies. The highest package was offered to him by Amazon company for an amount of Rs.44.14 lacs per year. He deposed that the injured would have had better opportunities had he not met with an accident resulting in amputation. He was duly cross - examined by learned counsel for insurance company. MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 4 of 25 BK Sh. Chandan Kumar Jha (Medical Record Keeper, Fortis hospital) was examined as PW-3(inadvertently mentioned as PW- 4). He relied on his authority letter as Ex.PW-4/1, detailed bill of the injured as Ex.PW-4/2 and discharge summary as Ex.PW-4/3. - examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company. Sh. Viplav Tyagi(Senior Prosthetic and Orthotist, P&O International Pvt. Ltd.) was examined as PW-4(inadvertently noted as PW-5). He relied on his authority letter as Ex.PW-5/1, his I-card as Ex.PW-5/2, original quotation as Ex.PW-1/4. He identified the quotation to be bearing signatures of Ms. Namrata. He deposed that the patient suffered elbow amputation and there is warrant of two years above elbow prosthesis requiring maintenance and replacement of battery and cosmetic glove. 8. Respondent no.3/insurance company examined Sh. Ashutosh Tiwari as R-3W-1. He brought the record pertaining to permit of offending vehicle bearing no. UP-16-ET-1197(dumper). He deposed that the offending vehicle was not having valid permit on the date of accident and the same was applied for renewal on 13.08.2018. He relied upon E-fee receipt dtd 13.08.2018 as Ex.R-3W-1/1 and Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 3 copy of permit dtd 14.02.2017 as Ex.R-3W-1/2. He was cross - examined by Ld. counsel for petitioner. Ms. Sneha Ghosh was examined as R-3W-2 by insurance company. She relied upon authority letter as Ex.R-3W-2/1, copy of insurance policy as Ex.R-3W-2/2(colly), notice u/o 12 Rule 8 CPC sent to owner as Ex.R-3W-2/3 and postal receipt as Ex.R- MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 5 of 25 BK 3W-2/4. She further deposed that as the offending vehicle was not having valid permit on the date of accident, so insurance company is not liable to pay compensation. She was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for petitioner. The deceased was 19 years of age and was student of B.Tec, Jaypee Institute of Information Technology, NOIDA and was also giving tuition and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. at the time of accident. It has been prayed that an Award as per his entitlement/claim be passed by the Tribunal, 11. The insurance company has argued and denied its liability on the ground that the accident did not occur due to rash or negligent driving and offending vehicle had no valid permit on the date of accident. It is argued that the petitioner was solely responsible for the accident. 16. On perusal of examination-in-chief by way of affidavit of PW-1, it is noted that PW-1/Petitioner deposed on the lines of petitioner's original stand as already noted above. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner/ claimant/applicant and against the MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 8 of 25 BK respondents.
texts.arguments: Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 6 of 25 BK to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & Ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge sheet against Respondent no.1 under Section MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 7 of 25 BK 279,304A,338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 15. Neither the driver nor the owner of the offending vehicle have entered into the witness box or raised any defence. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 19. The following observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited And Others (2018) 7 SCC 558 is relevant to the present facts and quoted as under: '...24. In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer. Therefore, the Tribunal MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 9 of 25 BK as well as the High Court had directed that the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver. The said directions are in consonance with the principles stated in Swaran Singh and other cases pertaining to pay and recover principle...''.. 20. In such circumstances, the liability of compensation falls primarily upon the driver and owner of the offending vehicle. Accordingly, in view of the settled law, the compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company/R-3 but with liberty to recover the same jointly and severally from the driver and owner of the vehicle in question i.e. Respondent no. 1 and 2. 21. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 10 of 25 BK some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 22. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 6 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure; (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising; (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability; (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 7 --Item (ii) (a). 23. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Neeraj Kumar P.No. 12 of 25 BK v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: "10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. What is required to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and upon Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 8 assessment of loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the standards multiplier method used to determine loss of dependancy). The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 32. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 12 Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording MACT NO:1073/18 Karan Malhotra v. Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 13 Neeraj Kumar P.No. 21 of 25 BK that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him. Karan Malhotra vs Neeraj Kumar on 23 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10344296/ 14
